items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: and he'd wait with his partner Beryl(?), who became his manager after he got his band later on...

ctx.x: It was on Powell just south of Geary -- on Powell Street. It was a big place.

And oh, it was really-really-really beautiful happenings then. We would go down to a place called... Oh, I can't think of the lady's name. Anyway, she had an after-hours place we used to go and eat, because she cooked these good hot biscuits. And Terry Gibbs was in the Army during that time. He had never heard anybody playing Bebop. He used to follow us around like a little kid. He'd pack his saxophone [sic?] around, whatever he needed to do at the time, just to be there to hear us place this music, you know. We…

We had a lot of nice times, all the guys would get up there and play. Because we were like the new thing, and the guys would hear you play and want to play with you. You know that routine, you know. Livin' fast...
